title: Simulation of a Pacemaker Circuit in PySpice

questions.q: How does an RC timing circuit work in a cardiac pacemaker?
questions.a: The capacitor charges exponentially through a calibrated resistor R1 until it hits a trigger voltage Vo after T = 60/BPM seconds, firing a discharge pulse into the heart load R2.

questions.q: Why is R2 (1 kΩ) much smaller than R1 (~752 kΩ) in the pacemaker circuit?
questions.a: R1 must be large so C1 charges slowly over ~0.86 seconds, whereas R2 must be small (1 kΩ) so C1 discharges rapidly in a few milliseconds to deliver a crisp pacing pulse.

questions.q: How do you calculate the timing resistor R1 for a heart rate of 80 BPM with C1 = 1 µF and switching factor 0.68?
What does resistor R2 represent physically in Experiment 6?
questions.a: R2 (1 kΩ) models the electrical impedance of the heart muscle (myocardium) across the pacemaker electrodes.

questions.q: What happens to the calculated R1 if the patient requires a faster heart rate (higher BPM)?
questions.a: A higher BPM requires a shorter period T = 60/H, so R1 must decrease proportionally to charge C1 faster.

questions.q: Why does the R1 formula in Experiment 6 independent of the supply voltage magnitude Vs when `switching_factor = Vo/Vs` is fixed?
questions.a: Because `Vo / Vs` is the dimensionless switching factor (0.68), so Vs cancels out inside `ln(1 - Vo/Vs)`.

questions.q: Which node holds the timing capacitor voltage and which node delivers the output pulse in Experiment 6?
questions.a: Node `'control'` holds the timing capacitor voltage across C1, and Node `'out'` delivers the pacing pulse across R2.

questions.q: What is the peak discharge current delivered to the 1 kΩ load R2 when Vs = 6 V and switching factor = 0.68?
Why would `math.log(1 - Vo/Vs)` raise a ValueError in Python?
questions.a: If `Vo >= Vs` (`switching_factor >= 1.0`), `1 - Vo/Vs <= 0`, which is physically impossible because an RC circuit fed by Vs can never charge above Vs.

questions.q: What is the discharge time constant when Switch S1 closes in Experiment 6?
questions.a: tau_discharge = R2 * C1 = 1 kΩ * 1 µF = 1 ms, which is ~750 times faster than the charging time constant.
